name: Phishing
example: Email claiming your bank account is compromised, urging you to click a link to "verify" your credentials.
signs: Sender address doesn't match claimed organization
Poor grammar/spelling (though AI is improving this)
Requests for credentials, OTPs, or payments
prevention: Navigate directly to websites (don't click links)
Report phishing to organization's abuse email
Use email filtering and anti-phishing tools

name: Smishing (SMS Phishing)
example: SMS: 'Your package delivery failed. Click here to reschedule: bit.ly/fake-link'
signs: Requests to reply with YES/NO or call a number
Claims from banks, govt, or courier services
prevention: Never click links in unexpected SMS
Report to 1930 (India) or carrier spam reporting

name: Vishing (Voice Phishing)
example: "Microsoft Support" calls claiming your computer has a virus, requests remote access.
signs: Demands for payment via gift cards/crypto
prevention: Hang up on unsolicited support calls
Never grant remote access to strangers

name: Ransomware
example: File-encrypting malware that demands cryptocurrency payment for decryption key.
signs: Ransom note on desktop or in folders
prevention: Disable macros in Office by default
Segment networks to limit lateral movement

name: Spyware & Stalkerware
example: App secretly installed on phone tracks location, reads messages, records calls.
signs: Unknown apps in device admin list
Phone feels warm when not in use
prevention: Install apps only from official stores

name: Trojans & RATs
example: "Free PDF Converter" installs remote access trojan giving attacker full control.

name: Social Engineering
example: Attacker poses as IT support, builds trust, then asks for password "to fix an issue."
prevention: Report suspicious requests to security team

name: Identity Theft
example: Fraudster uses stolen PAN/Aadhaar to take loans, open credit cards in your name.
signs: Bills for services you didn't use
IRS/Tax notices for income you didn't earn
prevention: Freeze credit if not applying for loans

name: Password Attacks
example: Credential stuffing uses leaked passwords from one breach to access other accounts.
signs: Password reset emails you didn't request

name: Fake Websites & Apps
example: Clone of bank website (bankofindla.com vs bankofindia.com) steals login credentials.
signs: HTTP instead of HTTPS (or invalid cert)
Poor design, broken links, generic images
No contact info or privacy policy
prevention: Check URL carefully before entering credentials
Use browser password manager (auto-fills only on correct domain)
Verify app publisher in Play Store/App Store

name: UPI / Payment Fraud
example: "Collect request" for ₹5000 saying "Approve to receive refund" - actually sends money.
signs: Requests to share UPI PIN or OTP
QR codes asking for payment to "verify" account
prevention: Never share UPI PIN with anyone
Verify collect requests in app before approving
Report fraud to bank & cybercrime.gov.in immediately

name: QR Phishing (Quishing)
example: QR code on parking meter flyer leads to fake payment page harvesting card details.
prevention: Preview URL before opening (most cameras show it)
Use QR scanner with URL preview
Don't scan random QR codes in public

name: SIM Swapping
example: Attacker convinces carrier to port your number, receives your 2FA codes, takes over accounts.
prevention: Set up port-out PIN with carrier
Enable SIM lock PIN on device

name: Deepfake Scams
example: AI-generated voice clone of CEO authorizes ₹2 Cr wire transfer. Video call with fake CEO.
signs: Requests to bypass normal approval chains
prevention: Establish secret passphrases for exec requests
Train finance/HR teams on deepfake risks
Use callback procedures for financial requests

name: Insider Threats
example: Disgruntled employee downloads customer database before resignation.

name: DDoS Attacks
example: Website overwhelmed by botnet traffic, legitimate users cannot access services.
prevention: Use DDoS protection service (Cloudflare, AWS Shield)
